activities.instructions: Work in one sitting. (1) Write Ohm's law as V = I × R and state in one sentence what each symbol means and its unit. (2) Work one example circuit with a single resistor: given any two of V, I, R, compute the third, showing the rearrangement each time. (3) Do two quick guided variations: one where you solve for current and one where you solve for resistance. (4) Transfer check: without looking at your notes, take a changed simple series circuit with one resistor and different values, solve for the missing quantity, and explain aloud or in writing why the relationship holds and what happens to current if resistance increases at fixed voltage. If you cannot do step 4 unaided, redo one guided variation and then attempt a second changed circuit once; stop after that.
activities.stoppingCondition: Stop once you have independently solved and explained one changed simple series circuit; do not add further practice sets or a separate final check.
activities.completionCriterion: You independently solve one changed simple series circuit for the missing quantity and explain the Ohm's law relationship and the effect of changing resistance, without notes.
